text: Large language models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on enormous amounts of text from books, articles, and websites. They learn patterns in language, not facts, by predicting the next word in a sentence. When you give them a prompt—a question or instruction—they generate a response based on those patterns. Prompt engineering is the skill of writing clear, specific prompts to get useful answers. LLMs can write, summarize, translate, and even code impressively well. However, they have limits: they can be confidently wrong, lack common sense, and cannot reason truly. They also reflect biases in their training data. So, while powerful, they are tools, not truth machines.
